## Changes since 9.3.0-dzbarsky37

- Avoid copying plain tokens in `ShellUtils.tokenize`; reuse a string builder only for quoted or escaped tokens ([c3e57f5a](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/c3e57f5a4b2ebab4702e6501b8e62d6eadadc5e6)).
- Reduce `PathCanonicalizer` memory by sharing a singleton node for non-directories instead of allocating a child map per file ([b2211293](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/b2211293ecca5058e63437ecbea2871f7dec2e00)).
- Filter toolchain dependencies in `RuleContext.Builder` without copying the dependency multimap ([8206e3b6](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/8206e3b6e538c5c87f082300e2c0383d1f486245)).
- Avoid traversing flag-alias maps when hashing `PlatformValue.Key`, while preserving the release branch's no-config options in key identity ([05ff55aa](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/05ff55aa08900d30f7706f80884bb5a72f3c5d35)).
- Reuse cached file digests for repository and module-extension watches. Include the prerequisite that reuses existing file metadata during digest-cache lookups instead of issuing another `stat` ([#31326](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/31326), [#30774](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/30774)).
- Make `bazel mod tidy` evaluate all module extensions and update dependency-only extension results and facts in the lockfile ([#31329](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/31329)).

### Compatibility

`bazel mod tidy` now evaluates extensions used only by dependencies and reports their evaluation errors. Before running it offline with `--nofetch`, use `bazel vendor` without target arguments to vendor the full dependency graph; target-based vendoring may omit repositories it needs.

### Validation

All 18 targeted test targets passed across the two backport batches, including the full `mod` and vendoring integration suites. The VFS and Unix filesystem suites were rerun successfully as a non-root user because their permission-denial tests fail under root. All 21 release-publication checks passed.

### Prebuilts

Linux and macOS binaries for x86_64 and arm64 are built and version-checked before immutable publication, with SHA-256 checksums and build-provenance records. Existing release tags and assets are preserved.
